journey.name: TL-17 An undo offer survives a trip to the editor and back
journey.description:
The list screen leaves the composition when the editor opens, which cancels the LaunchedEffect holding the snackbar - so neither of its branches runs, onMessageShown is never called, and the TaskDeleted message stays in the ViewModel state. Coming back re-runs the effect and re-offers the undo.
That is what this journey pins: the offer is not silently lost by navigating away, and what comes back is still actionable rather than a dead message. The list ViewModel is scoped to its back stack entry, so it and the captured task survive the round trip.
The neighbouring rule - a shown message is cleared so a rotation does not repeat it - is covered as state by the ViewModel test. Here the message was never shown at all, which is the case that rule must not swallow.
Preconditions: adb shell am force-stop com.rounds.test.to_dolist adb shell am start -n com.rounds.test.to_dolist/.MainActivity --es qa_failure_rate 0.0

actions.action: Tap the element with the content description "Delete task" on the "Book dentist" row
Verify that a message reading "Task deleted" is on screen
Tap the element with the content description "Add task" while that message is still on screen
Verify that the title "New task" is on screen
Verify that no "Task deleted" message and no "Undo" action are on screen
Tap the element with the content description "Back"
Verify that the app returns to the "Tasks" screen
Verify that a message reading "Task deleted" is on screen again, with an "Undo" action
Tap the "Undo" action on that message
Verify that "Book dentist" is on screen again
Verify that "Book dentist" is the last row in the list
